questions.question: It is given that $\sin\left(\dfrac{11\pi}{12}\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}$. Which of the following is the value of $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}\right)$?
questions.answer: **A.** $\sin\frac{11\pi}{12}=\sin\frac{\pi}{12}$ and $\frac{\pi}{12}$ lies in the range of $\sin^{-1}$.

questions.question: Which of the following could be one of the factors of the polynomial $P(x)=x^3+x^2-5x-2$?
The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown. Which of the following is a graph of $y=-\dfrac{1}{f(|x|)}$?
questions.answer: **B.** $f(|x|)<0$ for $|x|<2$, so the graph is positive there, with asymptotes $x=\pm2$. Since $f(|x|)$ has a cusp at $x=0$ and minima at $x=\pm\frac12$, the middle branch has a small cusp at $x=0$.

questions.question: Which of the following is the coefficient of the $x^3$ term in the expansion of $(2-x)^8$?
Which inequality below has the same solution set as the equation $|x+5|+|x-1|=6$?
questions.answer: **C.** The distances to $-5$ and $1$ sum to $6$ exactly when $-5\le x\le1$, which is $|x+2|\le3$.

questions.question: A team of $r$ student representatives is chosen from a class of $n$ students, where $r<n$. The team must include a captain and a vice-captain. In how many ways can the team be selected?
questions.answer: **D.** Choose captain and vice-captain ($n(n-1)$ ways), then the other $r-2$ members from the remaining $n-2$.

questions.question: The diagram shows the graph of $h(x)=\dfrac{g(x)}{f(x)}$. Which of the following best represents the graphs of both $f(x)$ and $g(x)$?
questions.answer: **A.** Both sides of the vertical asymptote go to $+\infty$, so $f$ touches the axis there (double zero) and $g$ is positive there. $h<0$ far to the left and $h>0$ to the right, so with $f\ge0$, $g$ is an increasing line.

questions.question: Which one of the following is $\sin^{-1}(\cos\theta)$, given that $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}<\theta<2\pi$?
questions.answer: **C.** $\cos\theta=\sin\left(\theta-\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\theta-\frac{3\pi}2\in\left(0,\frac\pi2\right)$.

questions.question: The probability of it being sunny on three consecutive days is $0.512$. The probability that it is sunny on exactly two days during a period of $n$ days is $0.0512$. Assuming the probability of being sunny is the same every day and days are independent, what is the value of $n$?

In parallelogram $ABCD$ shown, $|\overrightarrow{AB}|=8$, $|\overrightarrow{AD}|=5$, $\overrightarrow{CP}=3\overrightarrow{PD}$ and $\overrightarrow{AP}\cdot\overrightarrow{BP}=2$. What is the value of $\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AD}$?
questions.answer: **C.** $\left(\overrightarrow{AD}+\tfrac14\overrightarrow{AB}\right)\cdot\left(\overrightarrow{AD}-\tfrac34\overrightarrow{AB}\right)=25-\tfrac12\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AD}-12=2$.

questions.question: Solve $\dfrac{2x}{x+3}\le1$.
questions.answer:
$x\ne-3$. Multiply by $(x+3)^2>0$:

$$2x(x+3)\le(x+3)^2\Rightarrow(x+3)(x-3)\le0$$

So $-3<x\le3$.

questions.question: Find the Cartesian equation of the curve with parametric equations $x=2\cos t$, $y=2\sin t$, $0\le t\le\pi$.
questions.answer:
$\left(\dfrac x2\right)^2+\left(\dfrac y2\right)^2=1$, so $x^2+y^2=4$. Since $0\le t\le\pi$, $y\ge0$:

$$y=\sqrt{4-x^2},\quad-2\le x\le2$$

questions.question: Three men and three women are to sit at a round table. How many seating arrangements are possible if there are no restrictions?
Three men and three women are to sit at a round table. How many seating arrangements are possible if two particular women must sit together?
questions.answer: Treat the pair as one unit: $5$ units around the table give $4!$ arrangements, and the pair can be ordered in $2!$ ways. Total $4!\times2!=48$.

questions.question: Express $\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x$ in the form $r\cos(x+\alpha)$.
questions.answer: $r\cos\alpha=1$, $r\sin\alpha=\sqrt3$, so $r=2$, $\alpha=\frac\pi3$: $\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x=2\cos\left(x+\dfrac\pi3\right)$.

questions.question: Using $\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x=2\cos\left(x+\frac\pi3\right)$, solve $\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x=-\sqrt3$ for $0\le x\le2\pi$.
questions.answer: $\cos\left(x+\dfrac\pi3\right)=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, so $x+\dfrac\pi3=\dfrac{5\pi}6,\dfrac{7\pi}6$ and $x=\dfrac\pi2,\ \dfrac{5\pi}6$.

questions.question: Vectors $\mathbf u$ and $\mathbf v$ are given by $\mathbf u=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf v=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\4\end{pmatrix}$. Find the magnitude and direction of $\mathbf u-\mathbf v$.
questions.answer:
$\mathbf u-\mathbf v=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix}$, so $|\mathbf u-\mathbf v|=\sqrt{17}$.

Direction: $\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac14\right)\approx-14^\circ2'$, i.e. about $14^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis (bearing $104^\circ$).

questions.question: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac13}\frac{dx}{1+9x^2}$.
questions.answer: $$\left[\tfrac13\tan^{-1}3x\right]_0^{1/3}=\tfrac13\times\tfrac\pi4=\frac\pi{12}$$

questions.question: Differentiate $y=3x\sin^{-1}(2x)$.
questions.answer: $$\frac{dy}{dx}=3\sin^{-1}2x+\frac{6x}{\sqrt{1-4x^2}}$$

questions.question: Using the substitution $x=\cos\theta$, find $\displaystyle\int_{-\frac1{\sqrt2}}^{\frac12}\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx$ in exact form.
questions.answer:
$dx=-\sin\theta\,d\theta$; $x=-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\to\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}4$, $x=\dfrac12\to\theta=\dfrac\pi3$.

$$\int_{3\pi/4}^{\pi/3}\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}(-\sin\theta)\,d\theta=-\Big[\sin\theta\Big]_{3\pi/4}^{\pi/3}=\frac{\sqrt2-\sqrt3}{2}$$

questions.question: A direction field is to be drawn for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x+2y}{2y}$. Find the slopes of the direction field at $Q(-2,1)$ and $R(-4,1)$, and describe the line segments to be drawn there.
questions.answer:
At $Q(-2,1)$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{0}{2}=0$, a horizontal segment.

At $R(-4,1)$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-2}{2}=-1$, a segment falling at $45^\circ$.

questions.question: It is given that $\dfrac{{}^nP_{r-1}}{a}=\dfrac{{}^nP_r}{b}=\dfrac{{}^nP_{r+1}}{c}$. Prove that $b^2=a(b+c)$.
questions.answer:
$$\frac ba=\frac{{}^nP_r}{{}^nP_{r-1}}=\frac{(n-r+1)!}{(n-r)!}=n-r+1,\qquad\frac cb=\frac{{}^nP_{r+1}}{{}^nP_r}=n-r$$

So $\dfrac ba=\dfrac cb+1=\dfrac{b+c}{b}$, giving $b^2=a(b+c)$.

questions.question:
Use mathematical induction to prove that, for $n=1,2,3,\dots$ and $\sin2x\ne0$,

$$\cos2x\,\cos2^2x\cdots\cos2^nx=\frac{\sin2^{n+1}x}{2^n\sin2x}$$
questions.answer:
**$n=1$:** RHS $=\dfrac{\sin4x}{2\sin2x}=\dfrac{2\sin2x\cos2x}{2\sin2x}=\cos2x=$ LHS.

**Assume** true for $n=k$. For $n=k+1$:

$$\text{LHS}=\frac{\sin2^{k+1}x}{2^k\sin2x}\cos2^{k+1}x=\frac{\frac12\sin2^{k+2}x}{2^k\sin2x}=\frac{\sin2^{k+2}x}{2^{k+1}\sin2x}=\text{RHS}$$

So by induction the result holds for all integers $n\ge1$.

questions.question: Find the particular solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{xy}{x+2}$ that passes through $(0,-1)$.
questions.answer:
$$\int\frac{dy}{y}=\int\left(1-\frac{2}{x+2}\right)dx\Rightarrow\ln|y|=x-2\ln|x+2|+C$$

At $(0,-1)$: $0=-2\ln2+C$, so $C=\ln4$. Since $y<0$ at the initial point:

$$y=-\frac{4e^x}{(x+2)^2}\qquad(x>-2)$$

questions.question: The region between the graph of $f(x)=\sin x\cos x$ and the $x$-axis over $x\in\left[0,\frac\pi2\right]$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the volume of the resulting solid.
questions.answer: $$V=\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^2x\cos^2x\,dx=\frac\pi4\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^22x\,dx=\frac\pi8\int_0^{\pi/2}(1-\cos4x)\,dx=\frac{\pi^2}{16}\ \text{units}^3$$

questions.question: The diagram shows two squares $OABC$ and $ODEF$ with $OA=1$, $OD=2$ and $\angle AOF=\theta$, where $0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ$. Let $\overrightarrow{OF}=2\mathbf i$, $\overrightarrow{OD}=-2\mathbf j$ and $\overrightarrow{OA}=\cos\theta\,\mathbf i+\sin\theta\,\mathbf j$. Explain why $\overrightarrow{OC}=-\sin\theta\,\mathbf i+\cos\theta\,\mathbf j$.
questions.answer: $OC$ has length $1$ and makes angle $90^\circ+\theta$ with the positive $x$-axis, so $\overrightarrow{OC}=\cos(90^\circ+\theta)\mathbf i+\sin(90^\circ+\theta)\mathbf j=-\sin\theta\,\mathbf i+\cos\theta\,\mathbf j$.

questions.question: The diagram shows two squares $OABC$ and $ODEF$ with $OA=1$, $OD=2$ and $\angle AOF=\theta$, where $0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ$. Let $\overrightarrow{OF}=2\mathbf i$, $\overrightarrow{OD}=-2\mathbf j$ and $\overrightarrow{OA}=\cos\theta\,\mathbf i+\sin\theta\,\mathbf j$. Given $\overrightarrow{OC}=-\sin\theta\,\mathbf i+\cos\theta\,\mathbf j$, use vector methods to show that if the points $B$, $A$ and $E$ are collinear then $\cos\theta-\sin\theta=\dfrac12$.
questions.answer:
$\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{OC}=(-\sin\theta,\cos\theta)$, $\overrightarrow{OE}=(2,-2)$, so $\overrightarrow{EA}=(\cos\theta-2,\ \sin\theta+2)$.

Collinearity gives $\overrightarrow{EA}=k\overrightarrow{AB}$ for a scalar $k$:

$$\cos\theta-2=-k\sin\theta,\qquad\sin\theta+2=k\cos\theta$$

Eliminating $k$:

$$(\cos\theta-2)\cos\theta=-(\sin\theta+2)\sin\theta$$

$$1-2\cos\theta+2\sin\theta=0\Rightarrow\cos\theta-\sin\theta=\tfrac12$$

questions.question: A bottle of soda at $25^\circ$C is placed in a refrigerator with constant temperature $6^\circ$C. Its temperature $T^\circ$C after $t$ minutes satisfies $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=k(T-6)$, where $k$ is a constant. The temperature drops to $16^\circ$C after $30$ minutes. Prove that $k=\dfrac1{30}\ln\left(\dfrac{10}{19}\right)$.
questions.answer:
The solution is $T=6+Ae^{kt}$. At $t=0$, $T=25$ so $A=19$.

At $t=30$: $16=6+19e^{30k}$, so $e^{30k}=\dfrac{10}{19}$ and $k=\dfrac1{30}\ln\left(\dfrac{10}{19}\right)$.

questions.question: A man walks along a straight path at $1.2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. A searchlight on the ground $6$ m from the path is kept focused on him. At what rate is the searchlight rotating when the man is $8$ m from the point on the path closest to the searchlight?
questions.answer:
$x=6\tan\theta$, so $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=6\sec^2\theta\,\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$ and $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{6}\times1.2$.

When $x=8$ the distance to the man is $10$, so $\cos\theta=\frac35$:

$$\frac{d\theta}{dt}=\frac16\times\frac9{25}\times1.2=0.072\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$$

questions.question:
The rate of sales of a new toy is proportional to the product of the number of toys sold and the number in the target audience who have not yet purchased it. The target audience is $4$ million. $950\,000$ toys had been sold by 12 am on 1 October, and $3.5$ million by 12 am on 1 December.

Determine on what day the company sold to exactly half of its target audience.

You may use the result $\dfrac{1}{x(a-x)}=\dfrac{1}{ax}+\dfrac{1}{a(a-x)}$.
questions.answer:
Let $S$ be the sales in millions and $t$ the days after 1 October: $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=kS(4-S)$.

$$\int_{0.95}^S\left(\frac1{4S}+\frac1{4(4-S)}\right)dS=kt\ \Rightarrow\ \frac14\ln\left(\frac{S}{4-S}\cdot\frac{3.05}{0.95}\right)=kt$$

i.e. $\dfrac14\ln\left(\dfrac{61S}{19(4-S)}\right)=kt$.

1 December is $t=61$ with $S=3.5$: $k=\dfrac{1}{244}\ln\dfrac{427}{19}\approx0.012756$.

When $S=2$: $t=\dfrac{1}{4k}\ln\dfrac{61}{19}\approx22.86$ days.

So half the audience was reached on **23 October**.

questions.question: Triangle $PQR$ is isosceles with $PQ=PR$. A circle with centre $O$ and diameter $PQ$ cuts $QR$ at $X$. Let $\overrightarrow{OP}=\mathbf a$. Prove, using vector methods, that $X$ is the midpoint of $QR$.
questions.answer:
Let $\overrightarrow{OX}=\mathbf r$, where $|\mathbf r|=|\mathbf a|$, and $\overrightarrow{OQ}=-\mathbf a$.

$$\overrightarrow{PX}\cdot\overrightarrow{QX}=(\mathbf r-\mathbf a)\cdot(\mathbf r+\mathbf a)=|\mathbf r|^2-|\mathbf a|^2=0$$

So $PX\perp QR$. Then, since $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\overrightarrow{PX}+\overrightarrow{XQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{PR}=\overrightarrow{PX}+\overrightarrow{XR}$ with both cross terms zero:

$$|\overrightarrow{PQ}|^2=|\overrightarrow{PX}|^2+|\overrightarrow{XQ}|^2,\qquad|\overrightarrow{PR}|^2=|\overrightarrow{PX}|^2+|\overrightarrow{XR}|^2$$

As $PQ=PR$, $XQ=XR$. Since $X$ lies on $QR$, it is the midpoint.

questions.question:
Particles $P$ and $Q$ are projected from the same point $A$ on horizontal ground. $P$ is projected at an acute angle $\theta$ to the horizontal with speed $u\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, and $Q$ at an acute angle $2\theta$ with speed $2u\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Both land at the same point $B$. If $P$ takes $0.6$ seconds to travel from $A$ to $B$, find the time taken by $Q$.

For $P$ (do not prove): $\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}ut\cos\theta\\ -\frac{gt^2}{2}+ut\sin\theta\end{pmatrix}$.
questions.answer:
Times of flight: $t_P=\dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g}=0.6$ and $t_Q=\dfrac{4u\sin2\theta}{g}=\dfrac{8u\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}=4t_P\cos\theta=2.4\cos\theta$.

Equal ranges: $u\cos\theta\,t_P=2u\cos2\theta\,t_Q=8u\cos2\theta\cos\theta\,t_P$, so $\cos2\theta=\dfrac18$.

Then $\cos^2\theta=\dfrac{1+\cos2\theta}{2}=\dfrac9{16}$, so $\cos\theta=\dfrac34$ and $t_Q=1.8$ seconds.
